remediation.issue: The runtime dynamically executes a Python module from a sibling skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Use a packaged dependency with a pinned version, or verify the sibling module against a trusted hash before importing it.

content.user_title: Check Manual Trades Before Order Entry
content.value_statement: Manual trade decisions can bypass plans and risk controls. This skill checks local inputs and records a clear decision before broker entry.
actual_capabilities: Validates written-plan, predefined-stop, position-size, and risk-amount answers for actionable candidates.
Compares actual risk with planned risk using exact decimal validation.
Checks optional market-regime and circuit-breaker decisions from local files.
Detects recent losses from local trader-memory-core thesis records.
Produces GO, REVIEW_REQUIRED, NO_GO, or NO_ACTIONABLE_ORDERS decisions.
Writes local JSON, Markdown, and optional JSONL audit records.
limitations: It does not place, cancel, or modify broker orders.
It does not fetch prices, positions, account balances, or market data.
Decisions depend on accurate local checklist and upstream artifact data.
Thesis linking requires a compatible trader-memory-core sibling installation.

use_cases.title: Review a Manual Entry
use_cases.description: Check one planned entry against its written plan, stop, size, and risk amount before broker submission.

use_cases.title: Enforce Team Risk Controls
use_cases.description: Combine candidate checklists with local exposure and circuit-breaker decisions for a consistent pre-trade review.

use_cases.title: Audit Trading Discipline
use_cases.description: Retain decision records and checklist answers for later process reviews and strategy research.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Trade
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my local pre-trade checklist file. Explain the decision and list every failed or missing requirement.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one manual order

prompt_templates.title: Check Several Candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate all candidates in my checklist. Separate actionable entries from watchlist items and summarize each decision.
prompt_templates.scenario: Daily review of several trade ideas

prompt_templates.title: Apply Upstream Risk Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate my checklist with the local market-regime and circuit-breaker decision files. Highlight any upstream block or unknown value.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Auditable Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the discipline gate with thesis state, deterministic as-of time, report output, and journaling. Summarize decision causes and linking failures.

output_examples.input: A planned entry has a written plan, predefined stop, approved size, and actual risk equal to planned risk.
output_examples.output: GO: The actionable candidate passed the checklist and all supplied upstream gates.

output_examples.input: An actionable entry risks 750 dollars against a 500 dollar plan.
output_examples.output: NO_GO: Actual risk exceeds planned risk. Do not place the manual order.

output_examples.input: A watchlist candidate has no manual order intent.
output_examples.output: NO_ACTIONABLE_ORDERS: The candidate is recorded, but no broker action is authorized.

best_practices: Provide both planned and actual risk amounts for every actionable candidate.
Use current, trusted market-regime and circuit-breaker artifacts.
Review every non-GO reason before entering an order manually.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a missing upstream artifact as permission to trade.
Do not use watchlist decisions as order authorization.
Do not bypass a NO_GO result by changing checklist answers after the fact.

faq.question: Does this skill place trades?
faq.answer: No. It evaluates local data and produces advisory decisions for manual order workflows.

faq.question: Which candidate intents are actionable?
faq.answer: ENTRY_READY, ACTIONABLE, ACTIONABLE_DAY1, and MANUAL_ORDER are treated as actionable.

faq.question: What happens when required data is missing?
faq.answer: An actionable candidate receives REVIEW_REQUIRED when required risk data or upstream decisions are unavailable.

faq.question: Can it detect revenge-trading risk?
faq.answer: Yes. It can inspect local thesis records for losses within the configured cooldown window.

faq.question: What files does it create?
faq.answer: It creates a JSON report, an optional Markdown report, and an optional JSONL journal entry.

faq.question: Does it need network access?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow reads local files and does not fetch broker or market data.
